research_question: What is the marginal (not average) annual cost of administering one additional DAF account, by sponsor segment and balance band?
finding_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis: per-account DAF administration cost is dominated by fixed and step-fixed costs, so average-cost figures overstate the marginal cost of small accounts at large sponsors and understate it at small community foundations.
supporting_evidence: Nationals run at ~25–32 bps and community foundations at ~127–177 bps of DAF assets [S]; cost elasticity to scale 0.41 (nationals) vs 0.84 (CFs) [S]; tail CFs plausibly carry $1.2k–$4.1k of DAF admin per account-year [I in source].
alternative_explanations: Elasticities come from cross-sectional 990s, not time series; allocation rules (A/G/AM) are assumptions; affiliate-borne costs sit outside Part IX at Fidelity/Schwab/BofA.
recommended_additional_research: Obtain activity-level actuals from 3–5 sponsors across segments; estimate marginal cost curves by balance band and grant count; reconcile to audited opex.

research_question: What is the minimum viable staffing of a compliant DAF sponsor, given segregation of duties, legally competent review and seasonal (December) peaks?
finding_or_hypothesis: Observation: the median tail community foundation operates with 5 employees in total (all functions, not DAF-only) [S]; the 6–8 person floor used elsewhere is an unvalidated assumption.
supporting_evidence: Tail CF median 5 employees (IQR 2–9), median opex $630k [S]; Form 990 median loaded labour $38.87/h across 898 sponsors, $57–73/h at $250m+ sponsors [S]; Q4 carries 57% of contributions and 32% of grant dollars historically [S].
alternative_explanations: CF employees also serve non-DAF funds; outsourced administrators (Ren, FMR) absorb staff off the sponsor's 990; volunteer boards perform review work unpaid.
recommended_additional_research: Survey staffing by role (approval, reconciliation, service) with outsourcing disclosed; test separation-of-duties feasibility at 3, 5, 8 FTE; measure December overtime/temporary staff.

research_question: At what balance is a DAF account economically viable under asset-based, flat-fee and hybrid pricing?
finding_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis: under 0.60% asset fees, accounts below roughly $40k do not cover modelled fully-allocated cost; flat subscriptions shift but do not remove the gap, as challengers' price increases suggest.
supporting_evidence: Illustrative break-even $40,667–$45,333 at 0.60% against $244–$272 modelled cost [D from illustrative S]; 49% of sampled accounts were under $50k at end-2021 [S]; Daffy and Charityvest raised effective prices moving upmarket [S]; incumbents removed minimums in 2020 [S].
alternative_explanations: Cross-subsidy from large accounts or affiliated investment revenue may make small accounts rational to serve; cost figures are illustrative, not observed.
recommended_additional_research: Fund-level balance distributions by sponsor (Schedule D gives only aggregates); cohort retention and growth of small accounts; Daffy/Charityvest 990 Part IX decomposition.

research_question: Which recurring DAF operating practices are structural (law, custody, banking) and which are habit or legacy technology?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding (secondary): paper checks and history loss in migrations are classified as habit; manual review of IRS-listed public charities is 'mixed'; weak nonprofit leverage is structural.
supporting_evidence: Incentive classification table with red-team corrections [S]; check-only programs (BofA, DAFgiving360 per 2024 policies) coexist with 67% EFT at Fidelity [S]; AEF migration kept two years of history [S].
alternative_explanations: Checks may persist because many small charities lack bank-verified enrolment; history loss may reflect vendor contract terms, not habit.
recommended_additional_research: Time-and-motion study at one sponsor; charity-side survey of EFT enrolment barriers; contract review of export clauses in vendor MSAs.

research_question: How should DAF sponsor service and case work be organised (shared queues vs restricted investigation lanes) to minimise cost without weakening controls?
finding_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis: shared case concepts with separate lifecycles for complaints, reconsiderations and investigations reduce rework; raw contact-volume metrics misstate cost.
supporting_evidence: Complaint corpus: 117 of complaint/mixed records fixable, 47 structural, all critical records structural; 'no communication' on held grants is a recurring theme [S]; no top-20 sponsor publishes a response-time promise [S].
alternative_explanations: Complaint records lack denominators; logged-in service channels were not observed.
recommended_additional_research: Interview 3–5 sponsors on case routing; measure repeat-contact and resolution time; compare outsourced vs in-house service models.

research_question: Do asset-based and affiliate-linked fee structures change payout, pricing or willingness to redesign operations?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: the incentive is documented (RCF passes 98% of fundholder admin fees to Ren; Fidelity pays FMR amounts equal to admin fees; adviser fees are the largest, often uncapped, cost layer) but its effect on payout is unsupported.
supporting_evidence: Audited RCF and Fidelity statements [S]; adviser fees capped at 1.00% only at MS GIFT, DAFgiving360 and TIFIN Give, 0–2.00% observed [S]; 'asset-based fee alignment favouring retention' classified Mixed, Low confidence on effect [S].
alternative_explanations: Payout differences may reflect donor mix and sponsor type rather than fee model.
recommended_additional_research: Fund-level payout by fee model (evidence item 5 in the industry report); matched-cohort comparison of flat-fee vs asset-fee sponsors.

research_question: Where does AI create net value in DAF operations, and who is the economic buyer?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding (modelled): redesign beats AI-on-existing-workflow in most processes; inference cost is immaterial; shared AI only breaks even at network scale; the buyer is an administrator or platform vendor, not an individual sponsor.
supporting_evidence: ~$0.45 inference vs ~$83 reviewer time per heavy review [S]; shared AI platform breaks even in 43% of draws with the five largest nationals (16% calibrated), 0.4% for CFs under $250m alone [S, modelled]; $120k/yr AI product not fundable below ~$1bn DAF assets [I on S].
alternative_explanations: Model parameters (amenability, QA rate, redesign share) are assumptions; field evidence on DAF AI is absent.
recommended_additional_research: A measured exception, handling-time and QA study at any sponsor (the industry report's single most important missing evidence).

research_question: Is charity verification a commodity market or a licence-constrained one?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: eligibility data is commodity (IRS BMF, Pub 78, Auto-Revocation, OFAC upstream of every check), but enriched verification is licence-constrained: Candid's licence requires stopping all use on termination with no retention carve-out, while Rev. Proc. 2018-32 §8.01(2) requires grantors to retain the report.
supporting_evidence: Candid API licence terms (2026-09-14) [S]; Charity Check embedded in NPT, Foundant, Give Interactive, akoyaGO [S]; no top-20 sponsor embeds Charity Navigator ratings [S].
alternative_explanations: Executed customer licences may contain retention carve-outs not visible in the public template.
recommended_additional_research: Collect executed licence terms from 2–3 sponsors; ask counsel whether retention conflict is real; map who resells IRS data at what price.

research_question: What does each grant payment rail cost the sponsor (not only the nonprofit), per payment and per exception?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding (nonprofit side): ~$1–2 per $1,000 grant on free EFT rails, ~$5–8 by check, ~$32 on DAFpay at its 2.9% default; sponsor-side rail pricing (Chariot Disbursements, PayPal Grant Payments) is not public.
supporting_evidence: Nonprofit cost panel (33 entities) [S]; Chariot public pricing pages [S]; four rail camps (Fidelity EFT/Stripe, PayPal, Ren RDE, Chariot) [S]; checks voided at 90 days [S].
alternative_explanations: List prices differ from negotiated contracts; exception costs (returns, reissues, positive pay) are not in list prices.
recommended_additional_research: Obtain sponsor-side rail invoices; measure return, reissue and stale-check rates by rail; total cost per settled grant by rail.

research_question: Do sponsors apply controls beyond what law requires, and what do those controls cost in time and donor friction?
finding_or_hypothesis: Hypothesis: manual review of IRS-listed public charities and blanket officer review above dollar thresholds exceed the §4966 public-charity exception and Rev. Proc. 2018-32 reliance; discretionary holds (2026 SPLC) show sponsors also exercise non-legal discretion.
supporting_evidence: §4966 excepts grants to listed §170(b)(1)(A) charities and grantors may rely on IRS listings [S]; RCF officer review above $500k [S]; CA AG named Fidelity, Vanguard, DAFgiving360 as restricting grants; 16 AGs letter [S]; Fidelity states review may take 10+ business days [S].
alternative_explanations: Conservatism may be rational (reputational, AG and sanctions risk) rather than inefficient; listed-charity exception does not cover prohibited-benefit (§4967) risk.
recommended_additional_research: Counsel review of which controls are legally required vs voluntary; measure review time for listed-charity grants; catalogue published discretionary-grant policies.

research_question: Do DAF sponsors meet accessibility obligations behind the login, and what service levels do they actually deliver?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding (public pages only): 0 of 13 readable top-20 sponsors claim a WCAG level; colour contrast dominates automated failures; no sponsor publishes a quantified response time.
supporting_evidence: axe-core 4.9.1 scan of 37 pages at 13 sponsors (69.3% of top-20 assets) [S, executed by the source]; critical failures at 4 sponsors [S].
alternative_explanations: Automated checks find only part of WCAG issues; logged-in portals (where grants are made) were not tested.
recommended_additional_research: Consented logged-in audits with assistive-technology users; mystery-shopper response-time measurement; check for accessible statements and tax documents.

research_question: What are the measured cost, duration and data loss of DAF platform migrations?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: migrations happen (Ren iPhi lost 6 of 57 sponsors 2023–Nov 2026; all dated CF portal switches ended on Foundant), but no migration publishes cost or completeness; AEF's kept two years of history.
supporting_evidence: Attrition with Wilson interval 4.9–21.1% [S]; AEF two migrations and DonorCentral closure [S]; vendor templates allow batch export, not live integration; iPhi 15-day export window [S].
alternative_explanations: Small sample; destination choice may reflect bundled pricing rather than migration ease.
recommended_additional_research: Interview migrated sponsors (Arkansas, Acadiana, WaterStone); request migration statements of work; measure history completeness before/after.

research_question: Why do community foundations consolidate onto a few portal vendors, and what does CF DAF administration technology cost them?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: Foundant runs 361 of 803 CFs (45%); median CF IT spend is $17k–$116k; ~43% of mapped CF assets sit behind portal-only front ends with separate ledgers.
supporting_evidence: CF vendor map with 0/15 spot-check errors [S]; long-tail Part IX analysis [S]; ledger segment research [S].
alternative_explanations: Consolidation may be driven by bundled grants-management modules rather than DAF features.
recommended_additional_research: Survey CF technology budgets and contract terms; identify switching triggers; measure portal-ledger reconciliation effort.

research_question: What share of grants needs human judgement (exceptions), by sponsor type and payment class?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: no sponsor publishes exception rates, reviewer minutes or turnaround distributions; observable non-standard grants are ~2.5–3% of dollars at large nationals and far less by count.
supporting_evidence: 990 Schedule I/F analysis [S]; only 5 of 28 published turnaround statements are measured, all vendor figures [S].
alternative_explanations: Dollar share understates count share of complex but small exceptions; exception definitions differ by sponsor.
recommended_additional_research: Sponsor time-and-motion study with a shared exception taxonomy; publishable P50/P90 turnaround.

research_question: Should workplace and processor 'accounts' be counted with invested DAF accounts when sizing small-account markets?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: 79.5% of the 3.59m reported FY2024 accounts sit at 22 donation-processor sponsors holding 0.9% of assets; Givinga's 1.42m accounts average $1.37; processors do not count the same unit as sponsors.
supporting_evidence: DAFRC panel recomputation [S]; Givinga 990 unit definition [S]; corporate micro-giving products closed 2019–2023 [S].
alternative_explanations: Some processor accounts may be genuine employee DAF accounts; unit definitions are not disclosed.
recommended_additional_research: Publish a separate processor-account series; confirm Givinga unit; size invested accounts below $10k and $50k separately.

research_question: How do incumbents respond on price to digital-first entrants?
finding_or_hypothesis: Finding: incumbents removed account minimums in 2020 while early challengers moved from 'zero fees' to tiered or asset-based pricing upmarket; standard admin fees converge near 0.60% on the first $500k.
supporting_evidence: Fidelity, DAFgiving360, Charityvest start at 0.60%; RCF 0.65% with $250 minimum; BofA 0.90%; Daffy $0–40/month [S]; Vennfi seed 'zero fees' vs current Charityvest schedule [S].
alternative_explanations: Convergence may reflect cost floors rather than competitive response; investment-pool cost is as large a lever as admin fee (Fidelity pool range 0.015–0.55%).
recommended_additional_research: Fee-schedule time series 2015–2026 for top-20 sponsors and challengers; all-in cost including pools.
